stories.title: Revolut hands over customer KYC + Bitcoin transaction histories after a spoofed government-domain request
stories.summary: A request sent from a real government-domain mailbox passed Revolut's checks and produced disclosures that, per customer notices, included passports/IDs, selfies, addresses, IBANs and Bitcoin transaction histories. Revolut has called it a 'sophisticated external impersonation scam' hitting a limited customer set and says funds were untouched, but it has not published a count, market or the agency domain used. For builders this is a live test of how custodial crypto rails handle non-standard disclosure requests - and a reminder that 'govt domain' is no longer sufficient proof of origin.

quality.note: CoinDesk post (08:46:33 UTC) plus The Block. Revolut's own company comment in the CoinDesk article postdates the X post. Customer count/market still unspecified.

stories.title: Stacks says its Bitflow 'Stack Sats' BTC incentive campaign goes live 16 Sep
stories.summary: The official @Stacks account says the Bitflow incentive program - a 1 BTC/month pool where a $25 swap enters a daily BTC raffle - starts 16 Sep, on top of Stacks' pooled-Bitcoin-staking ('Genesis Bond') surface. The same day Stacks claimed Bitcoin staking is pulling in institutions and large BTC holders new to STX. It is a DEX incentive campaign, not a protocol upgrade or audit - the payout pool is small relative to BTC supply and the 'institutions are stacking' line is unsourced marketing.

quality.note: Official @Stacks announcement (17:47:01 UTC) with the live campaign page. Follow-up to the 11 Sep 'Stack Sats' program announcement already covered in the 09-12 edition.

stories.title: Catch-up: Nasdaq Ventures invests $100M in Kraken parent Payward for tokenized equities
stories.summary: Nasdaq's venture arm put $100M into Payward (Kraken's parent), reportedly pushing Kraken's valuation to ~$21B, to extend the Nasdaq Equity Tokens (NETs) collaboration and target 2027 tokenized-stock trading plus market infrastructure and surveillance. It lands 10 Sep - just outside the 30-hour window - and its canonical CoinDesk URL is absent from today's edition and archives. The 10 Sep event is the cleanest institutional RWA signal this week even if the X chatter about it is older.

stories.title: White House digital-asset director on the Sept 15 CLARITY Act cloture vote: 'bad day to be a Clarity Act doomer'
stories.summary: Bitcoin Magazine's X post quotes White House Digital Asset Advisory Council executive director Patrick Witt calling the sentiment ahead of the 15 Sep procedural/cloture vote 'a bad day to be a Clarity Act doomer,' while the vote still needs 60 votes and the Tillis-Gallego ethics compromise remains unresolved. The 15 Sep action is procedural, not enactment; a cloture failure would kill the bill for 2026 and, given midterm politics, likely until 2029. This is a second-hand quote, not a bill text drop - but it is the clearest in-window signal on where the White House stands.

quality.note: Witt's original X post not located in this sweep; the quote is second-hand via Bitcoin Magazine's screenshots. The crypto.news explainer (04 Sep) is the cleanest in-window written breakdown of the vote mechanics.

stories.title: Catch-up: StarkWare says Quantum-Safe Bitcoin is 'possible today on Bitcoin mainnet'
stories.summary: StarkWare posted a QSB promo on 12 Sep claiming hash-based quantum-safe outputs are 'possible today on Bitcoin mainnet' with no consensus change - coins moved into a QSB output are protected even if the public key leaks. The underlying mainnet event (first QSB tx, block 964,199) was 26 Aug and is not in this window; QSB does not make Bitcoin itself quantum-safe, it only protects coins moved into that specific output, and StarkWare still prefers a future soft fork. Worth a read if you are planning a QSB strategy, but this post is a recirculation of the August release.

quality.note: Official StarkWare X post with the dated blog. The underlying mainnet tx predates the window (26 Aug).

stories.title: Anthropic unilaterally commits to embedded third-party evaluators - 'We Must Pace the Frontier'
stories.summary: Dario Amodei published a long essay committing Anthropic to embedded third-party evaluators (e.g. METR) with permanent employee-level access to verify safety, report incidents and assess alignment of models and training pipelines, and arguing the pace of capability must be deliberately slowed given recursive self-improvement and the OpenAI-Hugging Face incident. @sama responded on X that OpenAI will also give independent evaluators employee-like access ('We'll have more to share soon'), and @ClementDelangue said Hugging Face is launching an Open Alignment Initiative led by Thomas Wolf and asked to join Anthropic's program. Caveat: the essay is on Amodei's personal site, not anthropic.com - @AnthropicAI and @claudeai did not post; the OpenAI/HF moves are verbal CEO commitments, not published contracts.

quality.note: Official CEO essay (posted 14:01:10 UTC) plus in-window verbal commitments from OpenAI and Hugging Face CEOs. Steps 2-3 of the evaluator program are proposals, not yet codified.

stories.title: Catch-up: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash is the smallest of the new architecture family with native vision
stories.summary: DeepSeek's official API changelog carries the V4.1-Flash release entry dated 10 Sep - a 552B-parameter MoE with native multimodal visual understanding, ~8B active parameters on input, 1M-token context and pricing built around low cached-input costs. It sits alongside V4-Pro at the top of the family and the company said it would route V4-Pro requests to Flash where appropriate. For builders: the release is outside the 30-hour window (posted 10 Sep ~06:00 UTC, just ahead of it), so this is a catch-up - but it is the cleanest new open-weights frontier-tier release this week and the official changelog is the canonical record.

stories.title: Qwen3.8-27B is now served on Cerebras (per @Alibaba_Qwen, 12 Sep)
stories.summary: The official @Alibaba_Qwen account confirmed on 12 Sep that Qwen3.8-27B is served on Cerebras's cloud (`qwen-3.8-27b`), with Cerebras quoting ~1,850 tok/s, an AA Intelligence Index of 34 and 64k/128k context on the public endpoint. For builders: the Cerebras endpoint is the cleanest way to run a dense Qwen3.8-27B at inference-class latency without the MoE routing.

stories.title: FANUC + Google: an 'AI Welding Agent' that reads a drawing and welds with zero setup or teaching
stories.summary: FANUC announced (11 Sep) an AI Welding Agent built on Google's Gemini Enterprise that reads an arc-welding component drawing, then auto-generates welding parameters (current/voltage) and the robot motion program - 'zero setup, zero teaching.' It demos at the International Welding Show in Tokyo from 16 Sep with shipments scheduled by end of December 2026; operators can still fine-tune the generated program, and the drawings are not used to train other customers' models. This is an industrial arm, not a humanoid - but it is the clearest 'drawings-to-weld' Physical-AI shipping product yet, and a template for how vision-LLMs will be folded into classic CNC/welding workflows.

quality.note: Official FANUC news release (11 Sep, date-only; noon UTC used) plus Nikkei Asia exclusive (10 Sep 15:01 UTC). No public weld-quality or cycle-time numbers; operator can edit the program.

stories.title: AgiBot ships GE-Act 2.0: a world-action model for manipulation that lifts G1-OP to 44.1% on zero-shot OOD tasks
stories.summary: AgiBot's official account (11 Sep) released GE-Act 2.0, a native world-action model trained from scratch on manipulation - no inherited video generator, no per-task fine-tune - scaling its data from 300 to 30,000 hours and using ~2,000 hours of failure/rollout data as training signal. G1-OP success climbs from 17.1% to 44.1% on 100 zero-shot out-of-distribution atomic tasks, and G2-90D adds +17.7 pp with <2% of co-training data. Paper is arXiv 2609.05588. Caveat: 44.1% still means most attempts fail, and the eval is AgiBot's own technical report, not a third-party benchmark.

quality.note: Official @AGIBOTofficial drop (11:27:47 UTC) with project page and arXiv paper (submitted 04 Sep, outside the 30h window - the X release is in-window). Company technical report, not third-party eval.

stories.title: Husqvarna gets the first FCC exemption for foreign-manufactured advanced robots (lawn mowers)
stories.summary: Swedish Husqvarna received the first conditional FCC approval for foreign-manufactured advanced robotics - its Automower 305/310/420/440 V IQ series - after the Defense Department decided they don't pose a national-security risk. It is the first carve-out from the foreign-robot rule announced in July, which has hit robot vacuums, pool cleaners and mowers. The FCC notice is dated 9 Sep (company PR 11 Sep 13:30 UTC; The Verge 12 Sep), so it is a 72-hour catch-up. It matters as the template for how the foreign-robot ban gets applied to specific, named hardware rather than by category.

quality.note: Company PR (11 Sep 13:30 UTC) plus The Verge (12 Sep 13:51 UTC). Underlying FCC notice dated 9 Sep - 72h catch-up, not a humanoid.

stories.title: Unitree G1 result: CAP learns to walk 'perception-blind' via continuously adaptive denoising (CoRL 2026)
stories.summary: A CoRL 2026-accepted paper (arXiv 2609.11553, submitted 10 Sep) reports CAP - a continuously adaptive, perception-blind humanoid locomotion controller that learns to robustly walk by denoising, validated on a real Unitree G1. It is a real-robot locomotion result aimed at robustness under sensory degradation (the 'perception-blind' framing means the controller keeps the robot walking even when perception fails). It is academic, not a company launch, and the G1 is a research platform - but perception-robust locomotion is a core open problem for anything that has to keep moving when a sensor drops out.

quality.note: arXiv preprint (submitted 10 Sep 13:45 UTC, inside the 72h window), accepted at CoRL 2026. Academic, single-platform (G1); not independently reproduced.

stories.title: FDA approves first therapy that directly targets muscle loss in SMA (Isembyld / apitegromab)
stories.summary: The FDA approved Isembyld (apitegromab-mstn), an anti-myostatin monoclonal antibody, for spinal muscular atrophy in patients 2+ already on an SMN2-targeted therapy - the first SMA drug that targets the muscle itself rather than SMN2. In the pivotal SAPPHIRE trial (NCT05156320), 10 mg/kg q4w slowed HFMSE decline vs placebo in ages 2-12, with clinically meaningful improvement in 34.2% vs 13.5%. Why a builder cares: myostatin inhibition is the exact muscle-sparing axis being tracked for sarcopenia and GLP-1-combo use, so this is the first approved in-class drug. Caveat: the indication is SMA on SMN2 therapy, not age-related sarcopenia; the label flags higher fracture risk (9% vs 2%) and the pivotal cohort was 2-21.

quality.note: Official FDA notable-approvals page (11 Sep, date-only; noon UTC) plus the @FDA post (12 Sep 14:10 UTC) and Scholar Rock IR. SMA, not age-related sarcopenia.

stories.title: Cell: fucosylated autologous bone-marrow MSCs - a first-in-human dose in advanced osteoporosis
stories.summary: A Cell paper (online 11 Sep, NCT02566655) reports a single IV dose of fucosylated autologous bone-marrow mesenchymal stem cells in 10 women with advanced osteoporosis - a glycocalyx-targeted approach that steers the cells to the bone. No serious adverse events; the authors report a large, durable drop in fragility fractures plus rises in osteoanabolic markers, bone tissue area and volumetric BMD. It is a Phase 1 safety trial with an efficacy signal, not a registrational RCT - the fracture reduction is against each patient's own pre-treatment history, with no contemporaneous control arm. It sits directly on age-related bone failure, which is a major fracture risk in longevity.

quality.note: Cell abstract page (11 Sep) surfaced via the official @CellCellPress post. n=10, no control arm; self-history comparison. Cell pages 403 to automated fetch, so the abstract line is from the @CellCellPress post + trial record.

stories.title: Science Immunology: an aged-lung STING adjuvant (AMnESTI) restores heterosubtypic flu protection in old animals
stories.summary: A new Science Immunology paper (11 Sep, Gao, Zhang et al.) shows that combining manganese with a STING agonist in alveolar-epithelial-cell-targeting nanoparticles (AMnESTI) reverses age-associated lung immune decline and restores heterosubtypic (cross-strain) protection from inactivated influenza vaccines. It is an animal (mouse) immunosenescence result - not a lifespan study, not a human trial - but it is a concrete gerontology-adjacent intervention aimed at aged lung epithelium rather than 'a better flu shot.' Caveat: STING agonists can drive systemic inflammation/interferonopathy, AEC targeting is a delivery claim, and restoring vaccine titers is not the same as reversing organismal aging.

quality.note: Science Immunology article (11 Sep, date-only; noon UTC) surfaced via an in-window X post. Animal evidence (mice); full abstract paywalled, mechanism from Science's blurb.

stories.title: Catch-up: PD-L2 is an immune checkpoint on senescent cells; blocking it cuts senescence burden in aged mice
stories.summary: A Cell Metabolism paper from the Kirkland group (first published 10 Sep - just outside the 30h window, so labelled Catch-up) shows PD-L2 is upregulated on senescent cells, letting them evade immune clearance; genetic deletion or anti-PD-L2 antibody blockade reduces senescent-cell burden and improves insulin sensitivity and grip strength in old mice, and circulating soluble PD-L2 rises with human aging and falls after senolytics. It reframes senolytics from 'kill cells with BH3 mimetics' to 'clear them via an immune checkpoint.' Evidence is animal intervention plus a human observational biomarker - not a human efficacy trial. Caveat: checkpoint blockade carries autoimmunity risk, and grip strength/insulin sensitivity are healthspan proxies, not lifespan.

quality.note: Cell Metabolism 'first published 10 Sep' (just outside the 30h window; 72h catch-up). Date-only; noon UTC. Animal + human-observational biomarker. Cell pages 403 to automated fetch; details from the journal RSS blurb + GEN + Cedars-Sinai PR.
